signals: Lecture was mostly history (student's own description); about 70% of the slides are narrative
Slide errors: 'Wein' and 'Stephan' misspelled; Wien constant written in 'mK' (meter·kelvin, not millikelvin); lava 'about 3000 °C' is well above real lava (roughly 700–1200 °C)
Slide 18 gives Planck's fitted h = 6.56e-34 J·s, not the CODATA value

fields.Front: What does the Rayleigh–Jeans law predict for blackbody energy density as \(\lambda\to0\)?
fields.SpeakFront: what does the Rayleigh Jeans law predict for blackbody energy density as the wavelength goes to zero?
fields.SpeakBack: it diverges to infinity; the ultraviolet catastrophe
fields.Elaboration: Experiment shows the curve peaks and falls back to zero.

golden.note: Angle 1 of 3 on the one concept this lecture teaches: the prediction.

fields.Back: Energy is continuous, so equipartition gives every standing-wave mode an average energy \(kT\)
fields.Front: Which classical assumption causes the ultraviolet catastrophe?
fields.SpeakBack: that energy is continuous, so every standing wave mode gets an average energy of k T
fields.SpeakFront: which classical assumption causes the ultraviolet catastrophe?

golden.note: Revision: the assumption, split from the mode count.

fields.Elaboration: Energy density = modes per volume × \(kT\), so it diverges as \(\lambda\to0\).
fields.Front: Rayleigh–Jeans: how the number of standing-wave modes per volume scales with \(\lambda\)
fields.SpeakBack: as one over lambda to the fourth
fields.SpeakFront: Rayleigh Jeans: how the number of standing wave modes per volume scales with wavelength

golden.note: Revision: the mode count, split from the assumption.

fields.Front: What did Planck change to fix blackbody radiation?
fields.Back: Oscillator energy is quantized, \(E=nhf\), so the average energy per mode becomes \(\bar E=\dfrac{hf}{e^{hf/kT}-1}\) and high-frequency modes are suppressed
fields.SpeakFront: what did Planck change to fix blackbody radiation?
fields.SpeakBack: he quantized oscillator energy, E equals n h f, so the average energy per mode becomes h f over e to the h f over k T minus one, which suppresses high frequency modes
fields.Elaboration: When \(hf\ll kT\), \(\bar E\to kT\): the classical result comes back at long wavelength.

golden.note: Angle 3: the resolution. The classical-limit Elaboration connects the two laws instead of adding a card.

fields.SpeakFront: the Rayleigh Jeans spectral energy density, u of lambda
fields.SpeakBack: eight pi over lambda to the fourth, times k T
fields.Elaboration: \(8\pi/\lambda^4\) counts standing-wave modes per volume; \(kT\) is the classical energy per mode.

golden.note: Now, not Core: exam-relevant but historical. Planck's full u(λ) is skipped as too long to recall usefully (canon 3).

fields.Back: an object that absorbs all radiation falling on it
fields.SpeakBack: an object that absorbs all radiation falling on it
fields.Elaboration: Its emission spectrum then depends only on its temperature.

fields.Front: Stefan–Boltzmann law: total intensity radiated by a blackbody at temperature \(T\)
fields.SpeakFront: the Stefan Boltzmann law for the total intensity radiated by a blackbody at temperature T
fields.SpeakBack: I equals sigma T to the fourth
fields.Elaboration: \(I\) is the area under \(R(\lambda)\). Doubling \(T\) gives 16× the power.

golden.note: The slide spells it 'Stephan'; corrected. 'Stefan–Boltzmann' and 'total intensity' in the prompt keep it apart from Wien (interference).

fields.SpeakFront: the Stefan Boltzmann constant sigma, three significant figures, in S I units
fields.SpeakBack: 5.67 times ten to the minus 8 watts per square meter per kelvin to the fourth
fields.Elaboration: Its units are power per area per \(T^4\), so it can't be Wien's constant, which is a length times a temperature.

golden.note: Checked against scipy.constants (5.6704e-8). The units in the elaboration are the interference guard.

fields.Front: Wien's displacement law (with the constant, 4 sig figs)
fields.SpeakFront: Wien's displacement law, with the constant to four significant figures
fields.SpeakBack: lambda max times T equals 2.898 times ten to the minus 3 meter kelvins
fields.Elaboration: Hotter means a shorter peak wavelength. The slide's "mK" means meter·kelvin, not millikelvin.

golden.note: Slide typos fixed ('Wein', 'mK'). The unit trap goes in Elaboration, not a separate card.

fields.Question: Peak wavelength of sunlight (solar surface ≈ 5800 K)
fields.Answer: \(\approx500\) nm, blue-green, near the middle of the visible band

fields.SpeakAnswer: about 500 nanometers, in the blue green, near the middle of the visible band
